topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines the primary learning outcomes, and establishes the clinical and biological context of cancer study.

topics.label: Biological mechanisms of cancer development and tissue modeling
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how cancer arises from genetic and epigenetic disruption of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture, alongside laboratory approaches for modeling these tumor cell behaviors.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and stepwise malignancy progression
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the histological and clinical characteristics of tumor invasion and metastasis, illustrating how benign precursor lesions progress in a stepwise manner into malignant disease.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and clinical mechanisms of morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: They define the naming conventions for benign and malignant neoplasms and explain the pathophysiological mechanisms through which tumor growth causes clinical disease and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across human populations and animal taxa
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the epidemiological patterns and mortality of major cancer types in humans alongside comparative oncology findings across companion animals and diverse multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Cancer screening principles and organ-specific modalities
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the clinical rationale, histological indicators, and practical effectiveness of population-level screening methods used to detect early-stage tumors across different organs.

topics.label: Lecture closing and practical preparation
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture by revisiting the learning outcomes and providing administrative guidance for upcoming practical sessions and lectures.
